Use this pathway after the normal electronics teaching and problem set. The notebooks support the circuit model; they do not replace deriving equations, building safely, or measuring a real system.

::: {.callout-note title="Current class position"}
Basic schematics and the five KCL/KVL questions are complete. Before circuit linear algebra, students learn the notebook workflow, core Python, NumPy arrays, plotting, documentation lookup, and evidence-based help requests. The bridge is **working code → controlled changes → NumPy investigation → documentation-driven repair → Kirchhoff equations → matrix model**. Capacitors and RC response follow this bridge.
:::

1. [Start with Python and JupyterLite](jupyterlite.qmd): run a cell, edit working code, preserve the notebook, and learn the browser workflow.
2. [Run Python and Jupyter on your own computer](local-python-jupyter.qmd): use a virtual environment in WSL, native Windows, macOS, or Linux instead of depending on JupyterLite.
3. [Complete Python and NumPy Foundations](python-numpy-foundations.qmd): practise variables, lists, indexing, loops, functions, arrays, filters, checks, plotting, and one documentation-driven repair.
4. [Find documentation and ask for programming help](finding-documentation-and-asking-for-help.qmd): reproduce an issue, search Python, NumPy, pandas, and Stack Overflow, and write a complete technical help request.
5. [Complete the two-loops-to-matrix assignment](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd): derive each loop equation step by step, build the matrix, and compare NumPy with an exact SymPy solution.
6. [Work through the Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd): apply the skills across KCL/KVL, graphs, data, investigation, RC, op-amps, and the calculus bridge.
7. Continue to [Python measurement logging](../linux-operating-systems/python-data-logging.qmd) and [analysis and curve fitting](../linux-operating-systems/python-analysis-curve-fitting.qmd) when the investigation needs repeated measurements or a fitted model.

::: {.callout-important title="Current assignment"}
Open [Assignment: Python and NumPy Foundations](python-numpy-foundations.qmd). Students complete a resistor investigation, use arrays and a function, make a graph, run assertions, and repair one intentional keyword error by reading the documentation. After this foundation, continue to [From Two Loops to a Matrix](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Core workflow"}
**Understand → Calculate → Build → Simulate → Measure → Verify → Investigate → Document → Share**

Most introductory notebook activities take about 15–30 minutes after the electronics calculation is complete. The [Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd) also defines multi-day investigations that can carry the electronics course while students wait for components, instruments, or soldered kits.
:::

The browser route does not require a local installation or a new account, but the school browser must allow JupyterLite and WebAssembly. Download work before leaving the browser.

Hardware remains valuable, but it is not assumed to be simultaneously available to every student. A simulation-first submission is complete when it meets the stated modelling outcomes and labels its evidence honestly. Measurements can be added later as a separate validation stage.
